epics.title: Epic 0.1: Repository scaffold
epics.intro: Monorepo skeleton: one `pnpm dev` boots web + api + local DB. See docs/system-design.md §3.1.

issues.title: Initialize pnpm + Turborepo monorepo with apps/ and packages/
issues.body:
## Context
Foundation for everything; layout per docs/system-design.md §3.1.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm-workspace.yaml` covers `apps/*` and `packages/*`
- [ ] `turbo.json` with `dev`, `build`, `lint`, `test` pipelines
- [ ] Root `package.json` scripts proxy to turbo
- [ ] `.gitignore`, `.nvmrc` (Node 20)

## Hints
Turborepo docs → "Getting started with existing monorepo".

issues.title: Scaffold apps/api: Express + TypeScript with modular layout
issues.body:
## Context
The modular monolith starts here. Modules live in `src/modules/<name>`; see docs/system-design.md §3.2.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Express + TS, `pnpm dev` hot-reloads (tsx watch)
- [ ] `GET /health` returns `{status:'ok'}`
- [ ] `src/modules/` exists with a README explaining module boundaries
- [ ] Error-handling middleware returns problem+json (RFC 7807)

## Hints
Keep it minimal — no DB yet (#7).

issues.title: Scaffold apps/web: Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind
issues.body:
## Context
Frontend app shell.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Next.js (App Router) + TS + Tailwind
- [ ] Home page renders project name + link to GitHub
- [ ] `pnpm dev` from root starts it via turbo

## Hints
`pnpm create next-app` inside `apps/web`, then wire workspace deps.

issues.title: Create packages/shared with zod and one shared type used by web AND api
issues.body:
## Context
Shared validation schemas are how frontend and backend stay in sync — core pattern of this codebase (docs/system-design.md §3.3).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `packages/shared` exports a zod schema (e.g. `HealthResponse`)
- [ ] api uses it to shape `/health`; web uses it to parse the response
- [ ] Type-checked end to end (`pnpm typecheck` green)

## Hints
Use `exports` map in package.json; no build step needed if consumed as TS source.

issues.title: Create packages/config: shared eslint, prettier, tsconfig presets
issues.body:
## Context
One source of truth for code style across all apps/packages.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Shared tsconfig base + eslint flat config + prettier config
- [ ] apps/web, apps/api, packages/shared extend them
- [ ] `pnpm lint` green from root

## Hints
Keep rules modest; strictness can grow later.

issues.title: docker-compose for local dev: Postgres 16 + PostGIS + Redis
issues.body:
## Context
Everyone needs identical local infra. PostGIS is required for geo search later (docs/system-design.md §4).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docker compose up -d` starts postgis/postgis:16 + redis:7 with volumes
- [ ] Ports/credentials match `.env.example` (#9)
- [ ] README section: prerequisites + how to start/stop/reset

## Hints
Use healthchecks so dependent tooling can wait.

issues.title: Add ORM (Prisma) connected to local Postgres + first migration
issues.body:
## Context
Migrations-from-day-one is a habit this project teaches.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Prisma configured against docker-compose DB
- [ ] An initial (even empty/placeholder) migration committed
- [ ] `pnpm db:migrate` script documented

## Hints
Schema for real tables comes in Phase 1 — don't model User yet.

issues.title: Root `pnpm dev` runs web + api concurrently; document in README
issues.body:
## Context
One-command local development.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm dev` at root starts web (3000) and api (4000) via turbo
- [ ] README "Getting started" section: clone → install → compose up → dev

## Hints
Depends on #1–#3 being merged.

issues.title: .env.example + env validation with zod on api boot
issues.body:
## Context
Fail fast on misconfiguration; never commit secrets.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `.env.example` lists every env var with comments
- [ ] api validates env with zod at startup and exits with a clear message if invalid

## Hints
Pattern: `const env = envSchema.parse(process.env)` exported from one module.

epics.title: Epic 0.2: GitHub configuration
epics.intro: Templates, docs and settings that make contribution self-service. Rules in docs/github-workflow.md.

issues.title: Issue templates: feature.yml, bug.yml, research.yml
issues.body:
## Context
Good issues are the engine of this project (docs/github-workflow.md §2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.yml`: user story, acceptance criteria, hints, files-to-touch
- [ ] `bug.yml`: steps, expected/actual, environment
- [ ] `research.yml`: question, deliverable (doc/Discussion), sources
- [ ] `config.yml` disables blank issues, links Discussions for questions

## Hints
Use GitHub issue forms (YAML), not markdown templates.

issues.title: PR template with test-plan checklist
issues.body:
## Context
Every PR answers: what, why, how tested (docs/github-workflow.md §2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` with what/why, test plan, screenshots section, checklist (tests, docs, self-review)
- [ ] Mentions `Closes #<issue>` convention

## Hints
Keep it short enough that people actually fill it.

issues.title: Enable branch protection on main (maintainer)
issues.body:
## Context
The golden path is enforced, not voluntary (docs/github-workflow.md §1–2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Require PR + 1 approval, required status checks (lint/typecheck/test/build), conversation resolution, no force push, admins included
- [ ] Screenshot of settings attached to this issue

## Hints
Settings → Branches → Add rule. Status checks appear after CI (#19) has run once.

issues.title: Create GitHub Project board with automation
issues.body:
## Context
Board = live state of the project (docs/github-workflow.md §2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Org-level Project: Backlog / Ready / In Progress / In Review / Done
- [ ] Workflows: item added → Backlog; assigned → In Progress; PR linked → In Review; merged/closed → Done
- [ ] Views: by milestone, by assignee, by area label
- [ ] All open issues added

## Hints
GitHub Projects (new), built-in workflows tab.

issues.title: Add CODEOWNERS for payments, auth and .github paths
issues.body:
## Context
Sensitive paths need maintainer review automatically (docs/github-workflow.md §2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `.github/CODEOWNERS` covers `/apps/api/src/modules/payments/`, `/apps/api/src/modules/auth/`, `/.github/`
- [ ] Owners = maintainer team/users

## Hints
Create an org team `@yrtai/maintainers` first.

issues.title: Enable Discussions with Q&A, Ideas, Show & Tell categories
issues.body:
## Context
Questions go to Discussions; issues stay actionable (docs/github-workflow.md §2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Discussions enabled, three categories configured
- [ ] Welcome post pinned: where to ask what, link to CONTRIBUTING

## Hints
Repo Settings → Features → Discussions.

issues.title: Write CONTRIBUTING.md: golden path, local setup, first-PR walkthrough
issues.body:
## Context
The single doc every new contributor reads first.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Golden path summary (from docs/github-workflow.md §1)
- [ ] Local setup steps (after #8 exists)
- [ ] "Your first PR" walkthrough pointing to CONTRIBUTORS.md (#18)
- [ ] Linked from README

## Hints
Write for someone who has never opened a PR.

issues.title: Add CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and LICENSE (MIT)
issues.body:
## Context
Standard open-source hygiene.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Contributor Covenant v2.1 as CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md with contact method
- [ ] MIT LICENSE with org name and year

## Hints
GitHub has built-in pickers for both.

issues.title: Create CONTRIBUTORS.md — every new member adds themselves as their first PR
issues.body:
## Context
Zero-risk first PR: fork/branch → add your name → PR → review → merge. This is the onboarding ritual.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CONTRIBUTORS.md with table: name, GitHub handle, focus area
- [ ] Instructions at top for adding yourself
- [ ] Linked from CONTRIBUTING.md

## Hints
Seed it with the maintainers.

epics.title: Epic 0.3: CI/CD
epics.intro: Red CI blocks merge — the quality gate that teaches discipline.

issues.title: CI workflow: lint + typecheck + test on every PR
issues.body:
## Context
The required status checks behind branch protection (#12).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on pull_request: install (pnpm cache) → turbo lint, typecheck, test
- [ ] Turborepo remote/CI caching configured
- [ ] Fails red on a deliberately broken test (prove it in the PR, then fix)

## Hints
`pnpm/action-setup` + `actions/setup-node` with pnpm cache.

issues.title: CI: build check for web and api
issues.body:
## Context
Catch build-only failures (env, next config) before merge.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `turbo build` job added to CI, green on main
- [ ] Build artifacts cached between jobs where sensible

## Hints
Extends #19.

issues.title: PR title linter: enforce Conventional Commits
issues.body:
## Context
Squash-merge uses the PR title as the commit message — titles must be conventional (docs/github-workflow.md §1).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Action validates PR title (`feat(scope): ...` etc.), fails with a helpful message
- [ ] Allowed types documented in CONTRIBUTING

## Hints
`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`.

issues.title: Enable Dependabot and CodeQL scanning
issues.body:
## Context
Security baseline (docs/system-design.md §8).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `dependabot.yml`: weekly npm + github-actions updates, grouped
- [ ] CodeQL workflow enabled for JS/TS
- [ ] Both produce at least one run

## Hints
Settings → Code security for CodeQL default setup.

issues.title: Auto-deploy main to staging (web → Vercel, api → Render/Railway)
issues.body:
## Context
Weekly demos run from staging; merge = deployed (docs/github-workflow.md §6).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Web deploys from main to a public staging URL
- [ ] API + managed Postgres/Redis deployed, `/health` public
- [ ] Staging URLs in README
- [ ] Env vars documented in `.env.example`

## Hints
Free tiers; managed Postgres must support PostGIS (Neon does).

issues.title: Vitest setup in api and web with one passing example test each
issues.body:
## Context
Testing infrastructure so every later issue can include tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Vitest configured in apps/api and apps/web
- [ ] One real example test each (e.g. /health handler; a component render with testing-library)
- [ ] `pnpm test` green from root via turbo

## Hints
Keep config in packages/config if possible.
